pages.title: Standard Math Library (<math.h>) and Linker Flags
pages.content:
### The `<math.h>` Standard Library in C

C provides high-performance floating point mathematical operations in `<math.h>`:

| Function | Prototype | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `sqrt(x)` | `double sqrt(double x)` | Computes $\sqrt{x}$ (requires $x \ge 0$) |
| `pow(x, y)` | `double pow(double x, double y)` | Computes $x^y$ |
| `fabs(x)` | `double fabs(double x)` | Absolute value for floating point numbers |
| `ceil(x)` | `double ceil(double x)` | Smallest integer not less than $x$ |
| `floor(x)` | `double floor(double x)` | Largest integer not greater than $x$ |
| `round(x)` | `double round(double x)` | Rounds to nearest integer |

### Linking with `-lm` in GCC:
On Unix/Linux/GCC, the math library functions are implemented in `libm.so/a`. You must pass the `-lm` flag to GCC at link time:
```bash
gcc program.c -o program -lm
```

callout.title: The -lm Linker Flag
callout.text: If GCC gives an "undefined reference to `sqrt`" error, add `-lm` at the end of the compile command.

checkpoint.question: Which GCC flag must be appended to link the math library?
checkpoint.explanation: -lm tells the linker to link against libm (the standard C math library).

callout.title: Memory Address Passing
callout.text: Passing `&x` passes the address by value. Dereferencing `*a` allows direct mutation of the original storage location.

checkpoint.question: Why does `void swap(int a, int b) { int t=a; a=b; b=t; }` fail to swap values in `main`?
options: Because the compiler optimizes away swap
Because a and b are local copies on the function stack; modifying them does not affect the caller
Because swap requires a return statement
Because temp is not declared static
checkpoint.explanation: In C, parameters are passed by value. Modifying local copies does not modify the original variables in the calling function.

msa.title: Module Assessment: Functions, Variable Scope & Recursion

questions.question: What is a "function prototype" in C?
options: The compiled binary code of the function
A declaration specifying the function's name, return type, and parameter types before its definition
A pointer to the main function
questions.explanation: A prototype informs the compiler of a function's signature so it can check calls for correct arguments before the function is defined.

questions.question: What happens if a recursive function lacks a valid base case?
options: It stops when memory reaches zero
Stack overflow causing a runtime crash (Segmentation fault)
questions.explanation: Without a base case, recursion continues infinitely until the call stack memory is exhausted, triggering a stack overflow.

questions.question: What is the lifetime of a variable declared with the `static` keyword inside a function?
options: The entire lifetime of the program, retaining its value between function calls
Allocated on the heap and freed automatically
Destroyed when the calling function exits
questions.explanation: A static local variable is initialized once and persists in the data segment for the entire program execution duration.

questions.question: What storage class is the default for local variables declared inside a C function?
questions.explanation: Local variables default to automatic storage duration (auto), allocated on the stack and destroyed upon function exit.

questions.question: How many base cases are strictly required for a valid recursive Fibonacci function $F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2)$?
questions.explanation: Since the recurrence references both n-1 and n-2, two base cases (n=0 and n=1) are necessary to terminate all branches.

questions.question: What keyword informs the compiler that a variable is defined in another source file or translation unit?
questions.explanation: extern declares the existence of a global variable or function defined in another translation unit without allocating new storage.

questions.question: What data structure is used by the operating system / runtime to manage function calls, local variables, and return addresses?
questions.explanation: The runtime call stack manages activation frames (stack frames) for nested and recursive function calls.

questions.question: Can a function in C return multiple values directly in the return statement (e.g. `return a, b;`)?
options: No; the comma operator evaluates both and returns only the last expression
Only if return type is multi
questions.explanation: In C, return statements only return a single value. Using comma operator evaluates expressions left-to-right and yields only the last value.

questions.question: What is the return type of a function that does not return any value to its caller?
questions.explanation: void specifies that a function yields no return value.

questions.question: What is the space complexity of a recursive function that recurses to depth $N$?
questions.explanation: Each active recursive call allocates a stack frame; recursing to depth N consumes O(N) memory on the call stack.
